content:
When meaning matters more than having the “perfect” reference photo 💙

Stephanie came to me with a vision for her father’s memorial tattoo - a blue retro Honda motorcycle with him riding toward the sunset, hair flowing in the wind. No helmet, just freedom. But she didn’t have the right photos to bring this vision to life.

That’s where the magic happened ✨

Instead of turning her away, we collaborated to CREATE the perfect piece. Using her motorcycle photo, online references, and digital composition and painting tools, we went back and forth through revisions until every detail was exactly right. The moment she saw the final tattoo? Age was was in tears “You know you did well because I’m crying. That’s my dad.”

This is what I live for - taking your meaningful ideas and stories and turning them into powerful art, even when you don’t have all the pieces figured out yet.

If you have a tattoo idea that means everything to you but you’re stuck on the “how,” bring me the WHY. Tell me what matters, what represents them, what captures their spirit. Through our consultation process, we’ll uncover exactly what needs to be in your piece to make it perfect.

Ready to create something meaningful together? Link in bio to share me your idea.

content:
Hello, my favorite tattoo people 🖤✨
2026 is officially my year of healthy change.

For the last 7 or 8 years, I think everyone in my life has heard me say, “Don’t worry, this is the year I’ll slow down a bit,” while never actually changing a damn thing. Well, I’ve finally hit my limit, and this year I’m truly committing to doing things differently.

I’m choosing to focus on my health, my happiness, and reconnecting with the inspiration that fuels my creativity. I love tattooing with my whole heart, and to continue loving it the way I do, for the long run, I need to make some thoughtful, intentional changes. Please read the slides above to see what those changes are! 

Thank you to every single client who has been part of this wild ride. I’m so grateful for you 🖤

• DOTBOT. SACRED GEOMETRY. DENVER’S OWN.

Jymi Calkins (@jymicalkins) is the founder of Long Live Tattoo Collective in Denver's Santa Fe Arts District, and he brings a music producer's sense of rhythm to every piece. Full Sail University, a background in music production, and a deep obsession with Sacred Geometry and Pointillism (Dotwork) — it all shows up in the work. His large-scale mandalas and Immersive Sleeves use high-contrast stippling to build real 3D depth, and his back pieces have been featured in Rooster Magazine for a reason. The kind of commitment-grade work that blends organic florals and rigid geometry in a way that shouldn't work as well as it does.

content:
🏆 Best in Show – St. Louis Tattoo Arts Festival ✨
This piece is based on a Namanari (生成) a character from Japanese folklore that’s basically a woman who’s still kinda human but already starting to turn into a demon.
It’s the first step in becoming a Hannya. She’s still got some human features, but emotions like jealousy, betrayal, or revenge start to take over and that’s when the transformation begins. You start to see the horns, fangs, and that eerie, powerful vibe that shows she’s not fully human anymore.
I really wanted to capture that moment where there’s still humanity, but something darker is coming through. The idea was to mix color realism with strong expression and a bold design that shows the inner change happening. 
Super grateful to bring home Best in Show with this piece. Big thanks to everyone who made it possible @villainarts @stlouistattooartsfestival @zen_ink_ @jaime.ortiz.tattoos @isabel_317 @jack_alfonzo28 @markos280297 
Using FYT needles @fytsuppliesusa_  @fytsupplies 
17mc Emerald, 7RL 35 HardLine, 9RS HardLine, 3RL Emerald
Using IKONIK - Premium Skin Care @ikonikcare 
Optik Glide during tattooing
Cosmik Soap after tattooing to wash the blood and plasma
Epik cream to moisturize the skin 
-
Esta pieza está inspirada en una Namanari un personaje del folclore japonés que representa a una mujer que todavía es algo humana, pero que ya empezó su transformación en demonio.
Es el primer paso para convertirse en una Hannya. Aún conserva algunos rasgos humanos, pero emociones como los celos, la traición o la venganza empiezan a apoderarse de ella y ahí es donde comienza el cambio. Empiezan a aparecer los cuernos, los colmillos y esa vibra poderosa y tenebrosa que muestra que ya no es del todo humana.
Quise capturar ese momento exacto donde todavía hay algo de humanidad, pero lo oscuro ya empieza a salir. La idea fue mezclar realismo a color con una expresión fuerte y un diseño que muestre esa transformación interna.
Muy agradecido de haberme llevado el B

content:
This is from a a photoshoot 1 month ago. Just got them back and had to post. When I see myself here compared to how I am today, I feel a lot of emotions. I see the scars up and down, and across my torso from all the surgeries. But what I feel the most is that I see myself and how strong I am and what I continue to overcome. A real example of how looks can be deceiving - what may appear fine on the outside is the opposite of what’s happening on the inside.

And that can apply to anything. So remember to be kind. The person you walk past today could be someone’s worst day, best day, last day — but the more important question is this: if everything were to change, right now, would you feel like you’ve truly lived?

I’m blessed to be able to say I have, and I want to continue to truly live this life by doing what feels is my purpose, which is to make other people happy. Something I can do with my craft, humor, empathy, understanding, compassion. 

🖤Remember that life is so short and don’t waste it on what ifs, or anything not serving you true happiness

content:
My dear friend @aidantattoos is one of the kindest people I know, and she wouldn’t ask for this kind of support herself, which is why I’m asking for her. Aidan was born with a rare condition called intestinal malrotation and has already gone through seven life‑saving surgeries since 2022. Those surgeries have meant losing her colon, appendix, cervix, uterus, and fallopian tubes, and now her gallbladder and right ovary are also failing and need to be removed.

Because her organs have been rearranged so many times, any incision on her torso is considered high‑risk. Even “routine” procedures are major operations that can lead to organ failure and sepsis. To stay alive, she has to travel out of state to top specialists who can handle cases as complex as hers, which means massive medical bills on top of flights, housing, and time away from work.

As a tattoo artist, if Aidan isn’t physically able to be in the studio, she doesn’t get paid. Right now, she’s facing more high‑risk surgeries and an unknown amount of time where she can’t work, while the bills keep coming. She has spent years taking care of everyone around her; now she needs her community to take care of her.

If you’re able, please donate or share her fundraiser—anything truly helps, whether it’s the price of a coffee or a full session. Your support will go directly to her surgeries, travel, recovery, and basic living costs so she can focus on surviving and healing, not on how she’ll pay her next bill. Link in stories / bio❤️

content:
Chicago was a blast, as always. This year’s Villain Arts Chicago Tattoo Arts Festival felt even bigger than I remembered, packed with so many incredible artists among the best of the best.

This year, I had the chance to work on an ambitious 3-day leg piece on an awesome client, Eve. She was an absolute trooper, sitting through 30 hours of pain over three days like it was nothing. We got most of it finished, and I couldn’t be happier with how it turned out.

The sheer amount of detail in this piece is what really makes it stand out. So many people stopped by the booth to check it out and show love, which meant a lot.

Unfortunately, we didn’t finish in time to enter Best of Show, but it was still worth the push. It was my first time attempting something this ambitious at a tattoo convention, and I’m proud of how far we got. Maybe next year will be different.

Overall, I had an amazing time and I’m already looking forward to the next one.

I’m pooped!!!

I’ve finally made my way through all new tattoo inquiries and everyone who submitted a request should now have received an email response from me. Some acceptance emails were sent out a few weeks ago, though I unfortunately never heard back from a handful of people. Because of that delay in communication, those clients can now only be scheduled from late August and onward at this time.

First and foremost, I just want to say thank you — truly. The amount of requests I received was incredibly overwhelming in the most humbling and beautiful way, and far beyond anything I anticipated. Knowing so many of you connect with and trust my work means more to me than I can properly put into words.

I also want to sincerely thank everyone for being so patient and understanding while I carefully went through each and every request individually. I never want anyone to feel rushed or overlooked in this process.

At this time, I officially have no remaining availability until the end of August and onward for the remainder of this year. content:
After careful consideration I’ve decided with deep contemplation to discontinue the Sak-Yant series. Nothing on anyone’s part, I just feel that people aren’t going to get the purpose of why I brought awareness to it. The practice itself will just continue to be abused as it’s such a social media trend. People are going to do what they do and I’m not one to control anyone’s choices. I will however say that when you play with sacred magic that doesn’t belong to you unfortunate things may happen and that was the choice you impulsively made, this goes to my own people as well. Even though you may carry the blood Sak-Yant is not a birthright, like I’ve said before it’s a privilege, a lifelong path and commitment. Not everyone can wear these tattoos. Not everyone can do these tattoos either, be weary of the fake tattooers that sell this practice off for a buck. Impulsive decisions begets regret. Research heavily on finding an Aja/Ajarn that comes from a lineage or has a master of their own and for heavens sake make sure they can read/chant the Sanskrit at least. 

Though I was designated for the path I personally chose not to follow it because of personal observations of spiritual responsibility before when I did practice/cast them. Instead I chose to walk my future path as a businessman and scholar. The practice is not a profit margin strategy as stated above. If you respect and honor it you won’t monopolize it.

Though it will be discontinued on social media I will still put ALL the information in my future books that I’m writing. I will also be dropping bits and pieces of its relation in some of my posts still but its focus won’t be there. These books are going to be me emptying my head of this encyclopedia of untapped Khmer knowledge in narrative to memoirs for my daughter. So, as of today it’s back to my normal posts of mythology and cultural preservation.

content:
Since the last tutorial study about waves another artist reached out to me to inquire about scales and the easiest way to do them. So I’m going to demonstrate it in two methods. One for Neak/Nak (Naga) and another for the Dragon. I use what I call the diamond armor method which derives from the name Yorn/Yant Grao Pich of Sak Yant. It was originally taught to me by a master in my past via medium of traditional Chinese/Japanese style technique. Once again, in respect I will not name drop here on social media 🙇🏻‍♂️

The technique starts with drawing parallel lines starting from the center of the serpentine body, the more rows the more scales you achieve. You can coil and taper it to work the direction of where the body moves. Next you start in the middle by drawing connecting repetitive “M’s” in one row. When doing this don’t think and just let your wrist go, your hand-eye coordination will naturally take over and make the scales naturally size itself or compress itself where needed. Then you continue in the next row with consistent “W’s” connecting all points to the existing “M” points creating what looks like diamonds. Again, let the pen take control of its natural flow no matter how off it looks. Like Bruce Lee says, “Don’t think, feel…” once you’ve done this for all rows you now have a diamond stencil to hardline your scales in, trust in following its pattern and you’ll be fine. If you stray off its guided path you’ll lose everything. Don’t overthink things when doing this also, just vibe deep into the method. Practice makes perfect and this basic fundamental technique can take you pretty far once mastered.

With dragons there will be a lot of tapers as opposed to the naga’s 2D strong stanced movement, one flows while the other is grounded heavy. The dragon’s scales are rounded and the naga’s scales are diamond pointed with bodhi leaf motifs in the center of each singular piece.

From a very young age, AG discovered a deep passion for art, developing drawing skills in a completely self-taught way and finding inspiration in classical art and illustration. While working to pay for university studies, a chance encounter with an artist who recognized potential in AG’s designs led to receiving a first tattoo machine — a moment that changed everything.
After losing that job, AG made the decision to fully commit to tattooing, starting from home and pushing forward despite limited materials and resources. Through discipline, consistency, and relentless practice, a solid foundation was built. This journey led to opening a tattoo studio alongside other artists and later continuing professional growth in Ecuador, where AG specialized in Black & Grey realism.
Today, AGTATTOOARTIS continues to evolve, driven by dedication, resilience, and a deep respect for the craft.

comments.text: Neo trad is just traditional but drawn way better lmao 😂

Neo traditional is creating lines that look like traditional line work after 20 years in the skin, traditional tattoos are done with a 3RL and a 5 rl. And in that frame work of those big bold lines you are able to create whatever you want and however you want it That’s neo traditional.

I feel this just highlighted a few elements used in neotrad styles but didn’t define a clear picture of what neo trad is. Let me try. I’d say on one end you have American traditional tattooing, bold lines, flat colour, stylied imagery. The other end you have realism, real world subjects depicted as they are in the real world. Now neotrad is the entire spectrum between these two worlds.

content:
Hello Friends and Family, It’s been a long time!

Next Saturday the 27th I’ll be hosting a fundraiser event to hopefully raise some money for my brother Cody Bollinger . Very unfortunately he was diagnosed with an inoperable brain tumor earlier this summer. Given the size and location of the tumor being very centralized it has caused several issues.  The main one being, is he has lost most of his motor functions on the entire right side of his body making just about impossible to his favorite things. Such as, riding bikes, playing darts/ video games ect. On top of that, a few neurologists have told him the won’t be able to work again for the foreseeable future and possibly not ever again if his symptoms don’t improve.

So with all of that said, this event is help raise some money to help him with his rent, food and general living expenses. 

In addition to me tattooing as many people as I can that day. We will have a few of my coworkers that we will have vouchers/gift cards available to be purchased, and then redeemed another day when each artist is available.

I will also have various prints I’ve drawn and custom stickers to purchase in case folks want to help but don’t want to be tattooed.

And last but not least I will be starting a raffle for one person to win a $700 dollar tattoo of there choosing! The tickets will be $20 a piece and the more you buy the more chances you have to win. This portion of the event will remain open for a few weeks so more people will have a chance to enter:)

I have added my Venmo QR code that you can scan to purchase any of these items and then I will transfer the money over to Cody’s account. Or of course any and all cash donations will go directly to him!

Please feel free to share this!

And ps, Cody will be at the shop Saturday afternoon hanging out as well:)

content:
• R E A P E R S •

Today marks @sevenreapers 3rd birthday. To celebrate, we thought updating everyone on the new location would be the perfect treat. Months and months of time, effort, hard work, dedication, help from friends, crash outs, hurdles, and a literal sea of @redbull later, we have done it.

Firstly need to thank our family from @bloombodyart and @qualitypiercings for taking care of us for the last three years, and giving us a special place to call home, get situated, and evolve. We truly would not be here with Matthew’s help, or his teams support.

Secondly, a HUGE thank you to @hopoffmy_johnson @noley_85 @tatfishbilly @nick___johnson for coming through with all the knowledge and abilities that I absolutely did not have in my bag. 

Thirdly, my girls. @jessi.deux has been an absolute rock, an irreplaceable help, and a hugely helpful guiding light. Clementine has been so patient, loving, and adaptable to the chaos that our schedules have become to make this happen. Of course, my mom coming to town to week help button everything up, take care of Clem, and help us settle in.

Of course, the @sevenreapers team has been an absolute dream through and through, and all of this is only possible because of them. They have trusted my vision, no matter how chaotic it has seemed, and continued to have faith in me. Thank you @adunning.tattoo @exhalenoelletattooer @stef_tattoos @trevorkopetattoos  and coming soon @beltanebeetattoo I love you guys so much, and can’t ever thank you enough for making all of this possible.

Lasty, our clients. You all have trusted and followed us no matter what, you’ve all been so accommodating to our schedules needing to change or adjust to work on the new space. We can’t wait for everyone to see it, and get tattooed here. New things will continue to be added over the next few months, and we will have a fun grand opening weekend later this year for everyone to visit.

Thank you all so much, this place means the world to me. I never imagine

April 2026 marks 25 years of tattooing professionally for me. I’ve now been making tattoos for over half my life! 25 years ago I committed to changing my stars. From college dropout, to union iron worker, to tattooer. To my friends and family, I may as well have been joining the circus. To me, a magical gift was bestowed upon me. The chance to practice alchemy of the skin. The stars seemed to align. I landed an apprenticeship at the only place I would’ve ever tried. Right place at the right time?? Maybe, but I also willed it to be with every fiber of my being. I was prepared to work harder than everyone. I was granted the opportunity to learn a craft that was handed down from mentor to mentee for generations. Lineages mattered. Trade secrets were just that… secret. The hidden knowledge of where to buy the right supplies and how to make needles wasn’t meant for everyone. It really was a magical time. I’m eternally grateful for the opportunity I was given way back then. I’m forever indebted to all of my mentors for taking a chance on me, Brian Flatoff, Jim Watson, Jack Mosher, and Kenny Melelu. Without the knowledge they shared with me, I wouldn’t be here today doing what I do. @holdfasttattooarizona has been my home for over 20 of those years. I can assure you, the magic still lives within those sacred walls. Many thanks to all those that have supported me over the years, especially @hollyween1031. You have to be a little crazy to thrive as an artist. Nobody knows that more than her. Thanks to everyone I’ve worked with over the years, and allowed me to gleen a little tat mojo. I carry it with me and promise to wield it wisely. Last but not least, thanks to everyone that’s ever allowed me to mark their skin indelibly. I wouldn’t be here without each and every one of you! The real secret is that it’s not just about the tattoos we make together. It’s about the stories we share and the life we live together. I don’t take any of that for granted. I’m rich beyond measure b

I've been tattooing for all of 13 or so years. Who can really count that high anyway. As you can see if you swipe over a few times, I specialize in bold black and grey tattoos. My main focus is heavy line work, illustrative designs in nature, and peppery dot shading.

⭐️ ANNOUNCEMENT • PLEASE READ ⭐️

I’m closing my private studio…
July 31st will be my last day in my private studio @agoodplacetattoospace 
Starting August 17th, I will be joining the amazing team at @sevenreapers new Tampa location alongside :
⭐️ @masonchimato 
⭐️ @exhalenoelletattooer 
⭐️ @stef_tattoos 
⭐️ @trevorkopetattoos

The last two years at AGPTS have been nothing short of amazing & healing. My private studio gave me the space to be myself, practice my craft, and step away from shop drama until I found the right space for me. 
However, I feel I have grown stagnant and lonely. 
I wish to rejoin my peers and break out of my current mold. 
At Seven Reapers, I will be surrounded by kind and talented artists I wish to continue learning from. 

July appointments will still be at A Good Place, appointments booked for August and going forward will all be at:

Seven Reapers
1906 N. Armenia Ave
Unit 207
Tampa, FL 33604

Thank you for all the constant support and love. 
I will treasure my Good Place memories forever and I appreciate every person who came to see my little space. 

I can’t wait for you to see the new one!

• R E A P E R S •

Today marks @sevenreapers 3rd birthday. To celebrate, we thought updating everyone on the new location would be the perfect treat. Months and months of time, effort, hard work, dedication, help from friends, crash outs, hurdles, and a literal sea of @redbull later, we have done it.

Firstly need to thank our family from @bloombodyart and @qualitypiercings for taking care of us for the last three years, and giving us a special place to call home, get situated, and evolve. We truly would not be here with Matthew’s help, or his teams support.

Secondly, a HUGE thank you to @hopoffmy_johnson @noley_85 @tatfishbilly @nick___johnson for coming through with all the knowledge and abilities that I absolutely did not have in my bag. 

Thirdly, my girls. @jessi.deux has been an absolute rock, an irreplaceable help, and a hugely helpful guiding light. Clementine has been so patient, loving, and adaptable to the chaos that our schedules have become to make this happen. Of course, my mom coming to town to week help button everything up, take care of Clem, and help us settle in.

Of course, the @sevenreapers team has been an absolute dream through and through, and all of this is only possible because of them. They have trusted my vision, no matter how chaotic it has seemed, and continued to have faith in me. Thank you @adunning.tattoo @exhalenoelletattooer @stef_tattoos @trevorkopetattoos  and coming soon @beltanebeetattoo I love you guys so much, and can’t ever thank you enough for making all of this possible.

Lasty, our clients. You all have trusted and followed us no matter what, you’ve all been so accommodating to our schedules needing to change or adjust to work on the new space. We can’t wait for everyone to see it, and get tattooed here. New things will continue to be added over the next few months, and we will have a fun grand opening weekend later this year for everyone to visit.

Thank you all so much, this place means the world to me. I never imagine

“What do tattoos mean to you?” I tend to get that question a lot and I think I have found the right answer that feels right for me.

So on a real note I never liked the way I looked growing up and struggled a lot with finding myself over the 28 years of my life. But I think for me tattoos are bodies of armor that are meant to make me shine brighter with each piece that is added on to my body. Tattoos have given me the confidence to really be myself and I feel like I’d be boring without them 😂 and huge thanks to @hollywills20 and her amazing photography skills for making me feel even greater!

What do tattoos mean for you?

🎬 REALISM AT FULL SCALE — CARLOS ROJAS IN PHILLY 🎬

@PhiladelphiaTattooArtsFestival brings in a heavyweight of modern realism with @crojasart. With 20+ years behind the machine, Carlos is known for high-impact color and black & grey photo realism — especially full sleeves and pop-culture portraits that read like cinematic stills.

His work first turned heads with hyper-detailed TV and film pieces, including a Breaking Bad sleeve that spread fast across the industry. Built on a fine-art foundation and sharpened through decades of tattooing, his tattoos balance smooth blends, hard contrast, and storytelling layouts designed to live large on the body.

Recognized by major tattoo media and a Season 9 Ink Master alum, Carlos delivers realism that holds up under close inspection and across time.
